analysis.title: The buying power nobody is talking about
key_insights: Broad equity positioning has fallen sharply from its mid-September peak per JPM's Panigirtzoglou, with institutional investors including hedge funds materially reducing exposure. This leaves more room for institutional buying than the price recovery alone suggests.

Vanda reports daily net call buying has rebounded above its one-month moving average after last week's sharp slowdown, following weeks of weakening institutional demand, particularly across AI themes.

Vanda reports hyperscaler call-put ratios rose above 2.0 this week with roughly $720mn in net call buying. Broad software is drawing fresh demand and semis are stabilizing, while AI software continues to lag.
The AI buying shift has not yet registered in one-month positioning indicators, which points to rotation within AI rather than a broad return of conviction.
JPM reports October inflows into leveraged equity ETFs were the highest monthly level on record, helping stabilize AI-related stocks. Retail is buying the correction.
Retail call buying has not meaningfully recovered since the June/July deleveraging. JPM sees scope for it to return into year-end.
QQQ short interest is at its highest level since 2023 per JPM. Some of it is hedging rather than outright bearish bets, but the short base is a potential source of buying if tech keeps recovering.
Tech companies have kept up share buybacks despite exploding AI capex. JPM notes repurchases remain resilient, though tighter financing conditions could eventually threaten that support.
Goldman notes November accounts for roughly 10.1% of annual buyback spending, second only to August. YTD repurchase authorizations are $1.34 trillion, up 14% y/y.
